title: Subjective Sleep Quality and Sleep Disorders in Patients With Severe Asthma
brief_summary: Bronchial asthma is characterized by the presence of symptoms that vary over time and of severity. Asthma symptoms tend to worsen at night and in the early hours of the morning, and the presence of nocturnal symptoms is an important indicator of therapeutic intervention in order to control the severity of the disease. Aim of the study is to investigate sleep disorders and quality, as well as and depressive and anxiety symptoms in patients affected by severe asthma before and after 6 months of treatment with monoclonal therapy. An observational, cohort, prospective, monocentric study will be conducted to evaluate subjective quality of sleep at baseline and post monoclonal treatment.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of severe persistent asthma
* Systemic steroids treatment for at least 6 months and/or ≥2 exacerbations in the last year
* Need to initiate monoclonal antibody therapy according to guidelines
* Age ≥18 years
* Signed Informed consent
* Patients able to collaborate in the required procedures

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of cognitive impairment
